messages:
alex_r: Quick sync — ACME asked for a per-route cost breakdown + error correlation view in Console by the end of Q2. They want to justify spend to procurement. Can we scope what 'MVP' looks like and call out launch criteria?

maria_p: Do we know which routes they care about? full request: 'per-route token cost, 90/99 latency, error-rate with stack traces (sampled)'.

alex_r: Yep, they listed a top-10 routes list. Also asked for ability to filter by model variant and time window.

samir: Core tradeoffs: 1) full per-token attribution needs route-level tagging in request path (lightweight) OR heavy sampling at dataplane. 2) error correlation needs trace hooks + payload sampling. Both add overhead.

jamie: Re: tracing hooks — adding a shallow hook to emit span id + route tag is cheap (~0.5–1% CPU). Automatic payload sampling + stack traces is the expensive part. We can do tiered sampling: 100% route tags, 1% payloads by default, 100% for enterprise customers on Dedicated.

alex_r: Proposed MVP (short):
- Per-route cost card (tokens * price) aggregated by day/week, filterable by model variant
- 90/99 latency and p95 token processing time
- Error rate with tied sampled traces (configurable sampling) and quick link to raw logs
- Acceptance: ACME can run query for their top-10 routes and see cost vs error trends for last 30 days, and export CSV

maria_p: That seems reasonable. Can we add an incremental rollout plan? ACME needs it in Q2 but we should avoid sweeping instrumentation changes.

samir: Rollout plan idea:
- Phase 0: route tagging only (no payloads) — emits route_id, model, prompt_size. Low risk.
- Phase 1: aggregated cost panel + latency metrics (no traces) — visible in Console beta for ACME
- Phase 2: sampled traces and error correlation (configurable per-org sampling) — GA after perf signoff

jamie: Agree. Also add a safeguard: if sampling spike causes >2% CPU bump on any host, auto-disable sampling and alert. ops-bot: note that as part of the feature flag config.

ops-bot: Alert rule created: "telemetry_sampling_cpu_bump" threshold 2%, notify #eng-oncall and #eng-platform.

liam: Question: how do we compute 'per-route token cost'? Do we derive from token counts + model price mapping in pricing service? Need clear formula.

samir: Formula: sum_over_requests(tokens_input + tokens_output) * model_unit_price_at_time_of_request. We need to join telemetry with billing model version table.

maria_p: That means we need timestamped model version metadata in telemetry stream. Is that already emitted?

jamie: We have model_version in the request envelope but not the pricing snapshot. We'll need a daily pricing snapshot join or annotate requests with pricing_id at ingress. Both are doable. Annotating at ingress is simpler for joins.

alex_r: Acceptance criteria (concrete):
- ACME can run Console filter "routes in [list]" and see a chart: cost / day, error rate / day, p90 latency.
- Clicking an error point shows up to 5 sampled traces with stack and request metadata (sanitized).
- CSV export includes columns: route_id, date, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_version, unit_price_usd, cost_usd, errors, p90_latency_ms.
- Performance: no more than 1.5% median tail increase in request latency in Phase 0/1; sampling must be gated by quota.

maria_p: Risks to call out to PM and stakeholders:
- Instrumentation churn on SDKs and dataplane (ingress annotation)
- Cost of storing sampled traces (retention and sampling policy)
- Billing alignment edge cases for model price changes mid-request window

samir: Mitigations:
- Keep default sampling low and org-configurable; retention TTL for sampled traces 30d; compress stored payloads; provide explicit doc for model_price join semantics (snapshot at ingestion).

alex_r: Do we have an owner matrix?
- Product: maria_p (ACME liaison + acceptance)
- Backend/Telemetry: samir (ingress tagging + join pipeline)
- Console UI: jamie (cards + CSV export)
- Infra/SRE: liam (CPU guardrails + alerting)
- Oncall automation: ops-bot (feature flag + auto-disable)

maria_p: Timeline ask from ACME: Q2 end. Realistic?

samir: With current bandwidth: Phase 0 + Phase 1 by Q2 end if we cut other lower-priority work. Phase 2 likely Q3.

alex_r: Decision: ship Phase 0+1 by Q2 for ACME beta. Phase 2 gated on perf acceptance and budget approval. I'll update the roadmap doc and flag scope cuts.

jamie: UX note: add a "why this route costs more" tooltip that surfaces token breakdown and model price — this helps ACME deck to procurement.

liam: I'll own alert runbook and rollback playbook for sampling.

maria_p: I'll draft the ACME acceptance test script and share in this thread by EOD tomorrow.

alex_r: Cool. Action items: @maria_p ACME test script, @samir ingress annotation PR, @jamie console mockups, @liam alert/runbook. Will mark the ticket P0 for ACME beta.

samir: One more thought — could we offer a lighter "cost estimator" widget for self-serve customers that doesn't need full instrumentation? Might reduce churn for small customers.

alex_r: Good idea, file a follow-up spike after the ACME beta.

maria_p: Thanks everyone. I'll post the acceptance script here and ping ACME once we have mockups. :+1:

alex_r: Thanks — closing thread for now.
